title: Fried Eggs
description: Fried Eggs are a timeless breakfast favorite featuring perfectly set whites and rich, runny yolks. Cooked gently over low heat with butter or olive oil, they deliver a delicate texture and are ideal for a classic continental breakfast or brunch.

ingredients.title: Ingredients (per serving)
items: 1 tbsp unsalted butter (or light olive oil for a lighter taste)
Salt, to taste (preferably flaky sea salt)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Optional: fresh herbs (chives, parsley, or tarragon)
Optional: a drizzle of truffle oil for a luxurious touch

ingredients.title: Equipment
items: Non-stick or well-seasoned stainless steel skillet

instruction.title: 1. Preheat the Pan
steps: Place the pan on medium-low heat.
Add butter and let it melt slowly, forming a thin foam without browning. This ensures gentle cooking.

instruction.title: 2. Crack and Prepare Eggs
steps: Crack each egg into a small bowl to check for freshness and avoid shell fragments.

instruction.title: 3. Cooking the Eggs
steps: Gently slide the eggs into the pan, keeping yolks intact.
Cook slowly on low heat for 2–3 minutes for sunny-side-up, until whites are mostly set.
For a slightly runny yolk with cooked tops, cover with a lid for 30–60 seconds to steam lightly.

instruction.title: 4. Seasoning
steps: Sprinkle salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Optional: add finely chopped fresh herbs for aroma and visual appeal.

instruction.title: 5. Finishing Touch
steps: Carefully lift the eggs with a spatula onto a pre-warmed plate.
Optional: drizzle a few drops of high-quality extra virgin olive oil or truffle oil.

instruction.title: 6. Serving
steps: Serve immediately with toasted artisan bread, sautéed mushrooms, or as part of a continental breakfast plate.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately with toasted artisan bread, sautéed mushrooms, or as part of a continental breakfast plate.

chefTips: Use fresh, high-quality eggs—this is the most important factor.
Cook low and slow; high heat makes whites rubbery.
For restaurant plating, use a ring mold to shape toast or sautéed vegetables elegantly around the eggs.
Experiment with finishing salts like fleur de sel for that delicate crunch.
